docs.title: Clichy
docs.text:
Clichy is an on-premise photo library built for the ECAM Brussels Distributed Systems project. It provides authenticated uploads, original/preview access, metadata extraction and exact/perceptual duplicate queries. Video processing and automatic blurry-photo detection are not implemented.

Start with local setup; Kubernetes is not needed for application development. Use testing before submitting a change, and the scripts catalogue to operate an environment.

docs.text: Need Read Understand components Architecture and application flow Understand public/private access Networking Prepare the server Kubernetes Follow a commit into Test/Production CI/CD Understand Citus and replication Databases Observe load and scale Monitoring Update an environment Deployment and migrations Investigate a failure Troubleshooting Decode a term Glossary

docs.title: Scope and academic evaluation
docs.text:
The cluster intentionally runs on one host, valtask. Configuration in Git is not proof of live operation; capture workflow runs and healthcheck output when demonstrating it.

Requirement Implementation and remaining evidence Tests, images and automatic Test deployment GitHub Actions tests/builds; GHCR SHA tags; self-hosted Test runner Production promotion and migrations Manual dispatch after Test; migrations before application rollout; GitHub environment protection depends on repository settings Sharding Target Test/Prod CNPG+Citus: userId, 32 colocated Photo/outbox shards; controlled cutover pending Replication CNPG: two instances; pre-cutover streaming confirmed by operator output; unified CNPG failover still needs a controlled test Rolling updates and scaling Deployments and Test API/Web HPA; zero downtime and scaling require measurements Monitoring Prometheus, API/worker/CNPG metrics and Grafana dashboard; verify scrape health Isolation and ingress Namespace-specific Secrets, Redis and storage; Traefik routes UI/API; Production tunnel is configured outside Git Known gaps No tested backup/restore automation, Test refresh/anonymization or replicated Redis; all data shares one physical host

docs.title: Application and photo processing
docs.text:
What is it? React Router renders the Web application; Fastify serves HTTP and Better Auth handles email/password sessions backed by Prisma/PostgreSQL. Redis is an in-memory data store; BullMQ uses it as a durable job queue with retries, rather than as a photo cache.

Why Clichy uses it HTTP requests record work quickly, while an independent worker performs CPU-intensive image decoding and produces previews.

docs.title: Upload to completion
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
  participant U as User
  participant API as Fastify
  participant DB as PostgreSQL
  participant Q as BullMQ / Redis
  participant W as Worker
  U->>API: POST /photos
  API->>API: Validate and store original
  API->>DB: Transaction: Photo + outbox
  API-->>U: 202 Accepted / PENDING
  API->>Q: Dispatcher publishes stable job ID
  API->>DB: Mark outbox published
  Q->>W: process-photo (photoId, userId)
  W->>DB: Atomically claim photo
  W->>W: Read shared original and generate derivatives and hashes
  W->>DB: COMPLETED or FAILED

The dispatcher retries unpublished events. Queue identity makes repeated publication idempotent; worker claims prevent duplicate processing. Queue defaults are four attempts with exponential backoff from two seconds. Invalid images and missing originals fail permanently. Stale PROCESSING records are recovered after 15 minutes and stale PENDING records after 10 minutes; normal SIGTERM lets the worker close within its 120-second Kubernetes grace period.

The original is written before the transaction. A process crash in that window can leave an orphan file; there is no orphan sweeper. Files and metadata must be backed up together. Redis AOF improves persistence but is not replication or a backup of the library.

docs.title: API and storage
docs.text:
The API accepts JPEG, PNG, WebP and GIF, with a 20 MiB multipart limit and a 40-million-pixel decoder cap. Sharp creates WebP previews, Exifr reads optional EXIF, SHA-256 identifies exact duplicates, and a 64-bit DCT pHash ranks similar images by Hamming distance. These queries do not imply a complete duplicate review or blurry-photo classification UI.

Route Purpose /api/auth/* Better Auth sessions and registration GET /photos, POST /photos Owned photo list and upload GET /photos/:id Original GET /photos/:id/metadata Metadata GET /photos/:id/thumbnail/:variant Preview GET /photos/:id/duplicates, /similar Owned duplicate/similarity queries DELETE /photos/:id Owned record and file removal

The API serves health at / and metrics at /metrics. Worker exposes /live, /ready and /metrics on port 3001; readiness requires Redis. Queue/storage configuration comes from the environment schemas; API and worker must agree. The backfill command reschedules incomplete photos across the library and therefore belongs to maintenance, not healthchecking.

docs.title: Traefik and Ingress
docs.text:
What is it? A Kubernetes Ingress declares HTTP routing by host and path. Traefik is the Ingress Controller that implements those rules.

Why Clichy uses it One application endpoint routes the browser UI and API to separate internal Services without exposing databases or Redis.

flowchart LR
  Browser -->|HTTPS| Cloudflare
  Cloudflare --> Tunnel[Cloudflare Tunnel]
  Tunnel -->|HTTP port 80| Traefik
  Traefik -->|/| Web[clichy-web Service]
  Traefik -->|/api/auth and /photos| API[clichy-server Service]
  Tailnet[Private LAN / Tailscale] -->|Test host| Traefik
Environment Host Intended access Dev clichy.localhost Local Kubernetes only Test clichy-test.home.arpa Private LAN/Tailscale Production valtask.xyz Public tunnel

Base Ingress uses class traefik, entrypoint web, UI /, API /api/auth and /photos. Namespace-local ClusterIP Services expose Web, API, Redis and the environment database. /metrics is not routed publicly by this Ingress.

docs.title: Cloudflare Tunnel
docs.text:
What is it? cloudflared opens an outbound connection to Cloudflare, allowing public HTTP traffic to reach a private server without inbound home router forwarding.

Why Clichy uses it Only Production is public. Cloudflare terminates HTTPS, redirects www.valtask.xyz to valtask.xyz and forwards the canonical route to Traefik over the tunnel. DNS, redirects and tunnel settings are outside Git.

Grafana (http://valtask:3000) and Headlamp (http://valtask:4466) use separate LAN entrypoints. They must remain private. Traefik ports are not automatically bound only to Tailscale; restrict access through the host firewall and verify existing SSH access before changing rules. See server setup.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
What is it? Clichy separates browser UI, HTTP API and asynchronous image processing. PostgreSQL stores records; a filesystem stores image bytes.

Why Clichy uses it Uploads can return promptly while a separate worker processes durable work independently of HTTP requests.

flowchart LR
  Browser --> Traefik --> Web[React Web]
  Traefik --> API[Fastify API and outbox dispatcher]
  API --> DB[(PostgreSQL metadata)]
  API --> Photos[(Shared photos PVC)]
  API --> Redis[BullMQ / Redis]
  Redis --> Worker
  Worker --> DB
  Worker --> Photos
  API -. metrics .-> Prometheus
  Worker -. metrics .-> Prometheus
  Prometheus --> Grafana

Web calls the authenticated API. API and worker mount the same photo volume at /data/photos. The API writes a Photo and an outbox event in one transaction; the dispatcher publishes that event to BullMQ. Worker jobs carry photoId and userId; queries include the owner/shard key.

Component Source Responsibility Web apps/web Login, dashboard and photo UI API apps/server Authentication, uploads, photo queries and outbox dispatch Worker apps/worker Metadata, hashes and preview generation Shared packages packages/db, auth, jobs, ui Prisma, Better Auth, queue configuration and UI components

The target Test/Production database is one CNPG primary with local Citus shards and one WAL standby, accessed through clichy-postgres-rw. Dev remains plain CNPG. The database guide distinguishes this repository target from the observed pre-cutover topology; the controlled migration preserves Test's separate existing dataset.

Namespaces isolate configuration and resources on one physical K3s host. Redis remains one instance per namespace. Shards, replicas and extra application Pods do not provide physical capacity scaling or host-level availability.

docs.title: Architecture decision records
docs.text:
Historical decisions remain available. Superseded records describe their original context; current targets and rollout limits are stated in ADR 0009.

  • ADR 0001: Kubernetes and environment namespaces
  • ADR 0002: PostgreSQL and Prisma
  • ADR 0003: Redis and BullMQ for photo jobs
  • ADR 0004: Historical Citus experiment
  • ADR 0005: Traefik as ingress controller
  • ADR 0006: Environment namespaces
  • ADR 0007: PostgreSQL replication and sharding scope
  • ADR 0008: Zero-downtime rollout is not yet verified
  • ADR 0009: Unified local Citus sharding with CNPG replication

docs.title: ADR 0001: Kubernetes and environment namespaces
docs.text: Status: Adopted in repository configuration; live operational status not independently verified.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The project targets self-hosted deployment on K3s and needs isolated Dev, Test, and Production configuration plus containerized services.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Use Kubernetes resources rendered with Kustomize, K3s for the on-premise cluster setup, Traefik Ingress, and clichy-dev, clichy-test, clichy-prod namespaces. Monitoring and Headlamp are separate cluster tools.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text: No alternatives are recorded in a formal ADR. Docker Compose is provided for local Postgres/Redis only, not as a production runtime.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: Kubernetes supplies scheduling, service discovery, probes and Deployment rollouts. Operators must manage cluster access, PVCs, secrets, ingress, and node/storage availability. Namespaces isolate names and configuration but do not provide separate cluster failure domains.

docs.title: ADR 0002: PostgreSQL and Prisma
docs.text: Status: Adopted.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The API needs relational persistence for identity, ownership, photo metadata, and processing state.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Use PostgreSQL with Prisma schema and committed migrations. Better Auth uses Prisma's PostgreSQL adapter. Each Kubernetes namespace has a CNPG-managed two-instance PostgreSQL cluster; application writes and Prisma migrations use its -rw Service.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text: No alternatives are recorded in repository history available here.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: Prisma provides typed data access and migration history. Schema migrations must be applied to independent environment databases before rollout and remain backward compatible with old Pods. CNPG replication is configured but not live-verified. Sharding, backups and Test refresh are not implemented; same-node instances do not provide physical host HA.

docs.title: ADR 0003: Redis and BullMQ for photo jobs
docs.text: Status: Adopted for asynchronous photo processing; operational baseline recorded at bce6e50, current live state not checked.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Uploads need image metadata extraction, hashing, and derivative generation without keeping the HTTP request open during all processing.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Use BullMQ backed by Redis. Server creates queue jobs; worker consumes process-photo; a PostgreSQL outbox stores publication intent and enables retry/recovery.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text: No formal comparison is recorded. Synchronous processing was avoided in favor of asynchronous work, based on current architecture.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: Retries, backoff, queue identity and recovery behavior are explicit. Redis remains a single instance with AOF/PVC, so it has no configured failover. Shared filesystem access between API and worker is required.

docs.title: ADR 0004: Historical Citus experiment
docs.text:
Status: Historical decision, superseded by ADR 0007.

The earlier experiment was abandoned after integration problems. That described an earlier architecture, not the current deployment.

At the time of ADR 0007, Test used a separate single-Pod Citus database for photo metadata and its processing outbox, hash-distributed on userId with 32 colocated shards. Dev and Production then used CNPG PostgreSQL without Citus. The separate Test CNPG cluster was retained for replication exercises and did not replicate Citus data. The unified target is now described by ADR 0009.

See sharding for current constraints and verification, and resolved incidents for recovery history. One physical host and one Citus process do not provide multi-node availability.

docs.title: ADR 0005: Traefik as ingress controller
docs.text: Status: Configured by K3s defaults and repository Ingress resources.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Browser traffic needs host/path routing to UI and API, while cluster services remain internal.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Use Traefik's traefik IngressClass; base Clichy ingress uses the web entrypoint. K3s installer retains default Traefik installation.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text: No controller comparison was found.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: K3s defaults make initial on-premise setup simpler. Hostnames, TLS, DNS and external exposure remain environment-specific; current Clichy Ingress does not configure TLS.

docs.title: ADR 0006: Environment namespaces
docs.text: Status: Adopted in overlays.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Test and Production need distinct settings, credentials and databases; Dev is configured separately.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Use namespace-per-environment with independent resources, Secrets, URLs and PostgreSQL databases. CI deploys Test before Production.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text: Separate clusters are not configured. No formal alternatives record was found.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: Namespace separation reduces accidental cross-environment naming/configuration overlap but shares the same cluster/node and does not guarantee resource/failure isolation. Test-to-Production promotion is ordered by workflow dependencies, but explicit application validation/approval depends partly on GitHub Environment settings.

docs.title: ADR 0007: PostgreSQL replication and sharding scope
docs.text: Status: Superseded target by ADR 0009. The topology below records the earlier decision; live cutover is separately gated.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Assignment asks for replication and sharding. The previous configuration used a single PostgreSQL StatefulSet. The educational prototype remains on one physical K3s node and does not need node-level HA.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Use CloudNativePG to manage two PostgreSQL instances per environment with asynchronous physical streaming, separate PVCs, automatic Pod recovery/promotion, and the -rw Service for application connections. Test additionally uses Citus with userId as the distribution key for photo metadata and processing-outbox rows. Dev and Production remain plain CNPG PostgreSQL. Keep replication and sharding as separate concerns. Do not scale database Pods directly.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text: A PostgreSQL operator is selected for physical replication. Multi-node Citus was deferred because it introduces worker membership and failure management. A single-node Citus instance in Test provides 32 logical shards and a low-complexity path to validate Citus routing. Synchronous replication is not selected because the prototype does not require zero data loss and asynchronous streaming avoids making writes wait on the standby.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: CNPG remains responsible for the replication exercise. Test Citus has one database Pod and no high availability; the CNPG Test cluster remains deployed separately. The 32 logical shards share one PostgreSQL process and host, so this is not multi-node capacity scaling or failure isolation. The data model uses compound keys containing userId, and outbox jobs carry that key so queries can be routed. Citus and Prisma migrations must stay aligned.

docs.title: ADR 0008: Zero-downtime rollout is not yet verified
docs.text: Status: Open evaluation criterion.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Kubernetes Deployments roll Pods, and deployment scripts wait for rollout completion. Default app replicas are one, and schema changes run before app manifests are updated.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Describe rolling update capability as configured but do not claim zero downtime without an observed test.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text: Multiple replicas and explicit rollout strategy can improve availability but must account for shared storage and database schema compatibility; no completed demonstration is recorded.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: A controlled deployment test with health checks, concurrent requests, metrics and a migration is needed before claiming the requirement is met.

docs.title: ADR 0009: Unified local Citus sharding with CNPG replication
docs.text: Status: Accepted target; repository implementation and local proofs complete. Manual Test cutover, CNPG certificate validation and controlled switchover remain required before Production. Supersedes the target in ADR 0007.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Test and Production use one CNPG cluster each, two PostgreSQL 18.6 instances, Citus 14.2, and 32 colocated Photo/outbox shards on userId inside the primary. WAL replicates shards and Citus metadata. There are no external Citus workers. Dev/local stays plain PostgreSQL. Retain namespace Secrets and existing PVCs.

Use a digest-pinned CNPG-derived image. Citus must preload first. Reuse CNPG's rotating streaming client certificate for Citus loopback connections, with explicit postgres/clichy mappings; do not weaken network SCRAM to trust. The CA is verified; loopback does not require a Service hostname certificate.

A new immutable migration aligns the old Production schema before distribution. Application releases wait for a manually acknowledged cutover and never roll the database image implicitly. Database image changes are explicit preparation operations.

docs.title: Feasibility and evidence
docs.text:
• Citus 14.2 source supports PG18 and a single-node coordinator.
  • Citus failure handling describes coordinator streaming replication and promotion.
  • CNPG 1.30 image requirements allow compatible PostgreSQL images and a primary/standby topology; image tags must expose the major version.
  • CNPG 1.30.1 configuration source preserves user preload order and defines the certificate paths, HBA rules and identity mappings used here.

These establish a viable design, not an upstream guarantee for the combination. Local image tests load Citus on PG18.6 and migrate Test/legacy Production as a non-superuser. They restore a logical dump, replicate over WAL, stop the old primary and promote the standby; existing shard IDs and application reads/writes survive. Test certificates are fixtures; the actual operator/Service/certificate lifecycle must still be verified on valtask. Native promotion is not a CNPG failover test. K3s 1.37 is tested but not officially supported by CNPG 1.30.

docs.title: Transition and rollback
docs.text:
The inspected old CNPG Test database contains a distinct user/photo/outbox row. Import active Citus rows/schema/history into a separate database, then retain the old CNPG database under a different name during cutover. Preserve every Prisma history row, including the rolled-back attempt. Logical dumps do not restore Citus catalogs; new migration 20261117140000 registers the restored canonical target. A later archive already containing that migration needs explicit reviewed SQL replay; migrate deploy alone cannot reconstruct missing distribution. Do not discard either original dataset.

Production conversion is in place and transactional, after backups and a write pause. A failed migration leaves its database transaction unchanged; Prisma failure history still requires diagnosis. After committed DDL, rollback uses a verified restore into another database and a controlled name switch, keeping the Citus-capable image. Never remove required binaries or discard post-cutover writes. The runbook defines checkpoints. Old standalone Test manifests are retained only until migration is verified; normal deployment no longer references them. Remove them in the cleanup checkpoint, while retaining the old PVC and backup for rollback.

docs.title: Local setup
docs.text:
What is it? Local development runs the Web, API and worker as Node processes, with PostgreSQL and Redis in Docker Compose. pnpm manages the workspace packages.

Why Clichy uses it Developers can work on the application without installing Kubernetes or accessing valtask.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Use Node.js 24, pnpm 12.8.1, Git and Docker with Compose. From the repository root:

pnpm install
pnpm db:start

pnpm install generates Varlock environment types. Compose starts PostgreSQL 18 and Redis 7.4; its password is for local use only. Do not copy production Secrets.

docs.title: Configure
docs.text:
Create these untracked .env files. The .env.schema beside each is the source of truth for required values and defaults.

apps/server/.env:

NODE_ENV=development
BETTER_AUTH_SECRET=replace-with-a-random-secret-of-at-least-32-characters
BETTER_AUTH_URL=http://localhost:3000
CORS_ORIGIN=http://localhost:5173
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres:password@localhost:5432/clichy?schema=public
PHOTO_STORAGE_PATH=./data/photos
REDIS_HOST=127.0.0.1

apps/worker/.env:

NODE_ENV=development
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres:password@localhost:5432/clichy?schema=public
PHOTO_STORAGE_PATH=../server/data/photos
REDIS_HOST=127.0.0.1

apps/web/.env:

NODE_ENV=development
VITE_SERVER_URL=http://localhost:3000

packages/db/.env:

DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres:password@localhost:5432/clichy?schema=public

API and worker must share the same database, Redis queue and resolved storage directory. Defaults are Redis port 6379, DB 0, no password/TLS and queue photo-processing. Set identical queue overrides in both services if needed. The local schemas already supply these defaults.

docs.title: Start
docs.text:
pnpm db:generate
pnpm db:migrate
pnpm dev

Open the Web URL printed by Vite (normally http://localhost:5173), sign up, then upload a small JPEG/PNG/WebP/GIF. The API listens on port 3000; the worker on 3001 for health/metrics. Expect upload status 202, then completed processing and available thumbnails. If Vite chooses another port, update CORS_ORIGIN.

Use pnpm dev:web, pnpm dev:server or pnpm dev:worker for one process. pnpm db:stop preserves Compose volumes; pnpm db:down removes containers and network, also preserving volumes. db:reset destroys the local database: it is not a setup or troubleshooting shortcut.

Workspace responsibilities: apps/web is React Router; apps/server is Fastify and the outbox dispatcher; apps/worker consumes jobs; packages/db, auth, jobs and ui hold shared database, auth, queue and UI code.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
What is it? Tests check behavior locally; type checking and builds verify workspace integration. They do not establish the health of a deployed cluster.

Why Clichy uses it CI must reject broken photo processing or incompatible changes before publishing images.

After installing and configuring, run:

pnpm check-types
pnpm --filter server test
pnpm --filter worker test
pnpm build
node --test packages/db/prisma/sharding.test.mjs infra/kubernetes/scripts/healthcheck.test.mjs

Server/worker suites use Node's test runner through tsx: storage, image processing, ownership queries/routes, outbox dispatch, metrics and job failures. Run a focused file with pnpm --filter server exec tsx --test src/image-processing.test.ts.

The shell tests mock kubectl: they exercise read-only behavior, missing components, timeouts, namespace isolation and exit codes without a cluster. To test all historical migrations plus Citus registration against the pinned image, with Docker available:

docker pull citusdata/citus:14.2.0
docker build -t clichy-cnpg-citus:18.6-14.2.0 infra/kubernetes/cnpg
CLICHY_TEST_CITUS=1 node packages/db/prisma/sharding.test.mjs

These tests create/remove disposable containers and an internal Docker network, without host mounts or published ports. They cover immutable migration history, legacy Production conversion, non-superuser SCRAM, certificate-authenticated COPY, logical restore, physical streaming and native PostgreSQL promotion. The latter is not an operator-managed CNPG failover test. Historical migration branches and invalid metadata remain covered. The integration case is explicitly skipped in the default offline test run.

For infrastructure changes, run bash -n on changed shell scripts, ShellCheck if installed, and kubectl kustomize infra/kubernetes/overlays/test (also prod and the separate database overlays). Rendering does not apply resources. Build this documentation with:

python3 -m venv /tmp/clichy-docs
/tmp/clichy-docs/bin/pip install -r docs/requirements.txt
/tmp/clichy-docs/bin/mkdocs build --strict

An upload smoke test writes application data. A healthcheck only observes state; keep these results separate when recording a demonstration.

Mermaid is pinned to 11.17.2. Validate rendering with that version; unescaped semicolons in sequence messages separate instructions and must be avoided.

docs.title: CI/CD
docs.text:
What is it? GitHub Actions executes workflow jobs; GHCR stores OCI container images. A self-hosted runner executes authorized deployment jobs on valtask.

Why Clichy uses it Tests and reproducible images precede deployment, with one immutable sha-<40-character-commit> tag tying migrations and images together.

flowchart TD
  Change[Push / PR / manual dispatch] --> CI[Types, tests and builds]
  CI --> Images[Build application and database images]
  Images -->|PR| End[No publication or deployment]
  Images -->|master push or dispatch| GHCR[Login and publish exact SHA tags]
  GHCR --> Test[Verify valtask and SHA; migrate; deploy Test]
  Test --> Gate{Manual dispatch with deploy_prod=true?}
  Gate -->|yes| Production[GitHub production environment; migrate; deploy same SHA]

The single source is .github/workflows/ci-cd.yml. Pushes/PRs target master. CI uses Node 24, pnpm's frozen lockfile, type checks, server/worker tests, Citus migration integration tests in a disposable Docker container, healthcheck regression tests and builds. Packaging builds the three application images and the CNPG+Citus image from infra/; only master pushes or manual dispatches publish images.

Test deploys automatically after successful CI/package. Production additionally requires workflow_dispatch with deploy_prod=true, successful Test deployment and GitHub Environment production. Approval rules are repository settings, not guaranteed by the YAML. Pull requests never run on the deployment runner. Jobs serialize deployments per environment. There is no automatic rollback or end-to-end smoke-test gate.

docs.title: Runner setup
docs.text:
Register a non-root Linux runner using Settings → Actions → Runners and the registration commands/token GitHub supplies. Give it labels self-hosted, linux, install its service using the supplied svc.sh, and provide Node 24, pnpm, kubectl, Git and access to GHCR and the cluster. Do not run untrusted PR code with these credentials.

The workflow explicitly uses KUBECONFIG=/home/valatras/.kube/config. The runner account must be able to read that protected kubeconfig; a different account/path requires a deliberate workflow update. Keep mode 0600 and verify access as the actual runner account. Runner credentials are distinct from each namespace's ghcr-pull-secret.

Deployment checks the checked-out SHA, image tag and single node valtask. The database workspace is installed from that same commit. Migrations run before new application manifests; failed migrations stop deployment. See the deployment runbook for operator commands.

Database preparation renders an immutable 18.6-citus14.2.0-sha-<commit> image separately from application rollouts. During transition, releases require the manual database-architecture acknowledgement; see the cutover runbook. No pipeline job imports a database or silently selects the old Test CNPG dataset.

docs.title: PostgreSQL, Citus and CloudNativePG
docs.text:
What is it? PostgreSQL stores relational data; Citus adds logical hash shards. CloudNativePG (CNPG) manages the PostgreSQL primary, standby and role Services.

Why Clichy uses it Test and Production target the same schema and topology: 32 photo/outbox shards inside one writable PostgreSQL instance, physically replicated to a standby. This combines sharding and replication without worker groups.

docs.title: Architecture and rollout status
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  App[API / Prisma / worker] --> RW[CNPG read-write Service]
  RW --> Primary[Primary: PostgreSQL 18.6 + Citus 14.2]
  Primary --> Shards[Photo and outbox: 32 shards each on userId]
  Primary --> Users[user: reference table]
  Primary -->|WAL: rows, shard tables and Citus catalogs| Standby[Standby: same Citus binaries and replicated shards]
  Primary --> PV1[(Primary PVC)]
  Standby --> PV2[(Standby PVC)]
  Operator[CNPG 1.30.1] -. supervises and promotes .-> Standby

This is the repository target, not a claim that cutover already happened. The operator's 2026-11-17 read-only output confirmed:

Source Observed state before cutover Active Test Standalone PostgreSQL 18.4/Citus 14.2; correct 32 colocated shards; zero users/photos/outbox rows Existing Test CNPG PostgreSQL 18.6, two streaming instances; a different database with one user/photo/outbox row and three migrations Production PostgreSQL 18.6, two streaming CNPG instances; no Citus; zero users/photos/outbox rows; single-column primary keys

These databases are not interchangeable. Test import must preserve the old CNPG database separately, including its migration history; never merge or overwrite it based on the active Citus database's empty row count. The controlled procedure is mandatory.

docs.title: Citus: logical sharding
docs.text:
What is it? Citus routes rows by a distribution key. Colocation aligns the shard layout of related tables; reference tables support shared identity data.

Why Clichy uses it Photo and PhotoProcessingOutbox belong to users and can share userId routing and foreign-key enforcement in both environments.

Each table uses hash(userId), 32 shards and the same positive colocation ID. user is a reference table (n/t, one shard). Compound primary/unique keys include userId. Outbox references Photo(userId,id); Photo-to-user delete is RESTRICT, outbox-to-photo delete is CASCADE, and both FK updates are RESTRICT. Images remain on the existing shared photos PVC. Existing coordinator-local auth-table registrations can remain in Test; they are not hash shards and are not converted or discarded.

Only the local coordinator (localhost:5432, group 0) stores shards. WAL copies its catalogs and physical shard tables together. After promotion localhost means the promoted instance, so no external worker addresses need rewriting. Application connections use clichy-postgres-rw; do not point them at individual Pods.

docs.title: Image, initialization and Prisma
docs.text:
The Dockerfile under infra/kubernetes/cnpg pins the CNPG PostgreSQL 18.6 image and official Citus 14.2 image by digest, on Debian 13/PG18. It copies extension files rather than PostgreSQL executables, installs pinned libcurl and verifies runtime linkage. CI tests it and publishes a PG-major-prefixed SHA tag. This is a locally tested custom integration, not a vendor certification of Citus/CNPG.

CNPG preloads Citus first, enables 100 prepared transactions and creates the extension through privileged bootstrap SQL on fresh clusters. Existing clusters need the explicitly approved extension step in the runbook; bootstrap SQL is not replayed on existing databases. The application role remains non-superuser.

Citus COPY and some parallel queries open internal connections. Loopback-only hostssl rules authenticate the existing CNPG streaming client certificate with explicit mappings to postgres/clichy. citus.node_conninfo verifies the server CA; verify-ca is used because the endpoint is localhost, not a Service DNS identity. External clients retain SCRAM. No passwords are copied into SQL or pgpass files, and certificate rotation remains CNPG-managed. Actual CNPG certificate integration still needs the Test checkpoint before Production.

Applied Prisma migrations are unchanged. New migration 20261117140000_unified_cnpg_citus aligns Production's legacy keys, backfills nullable outbox owners, removes incompatible global uniqueness and registers missing tables transactionally. Existing correct Test shards are only validated. Unexpected metadata or orphan rows fail; no destructive conversion runs automatically. Dev/local PostgreSQL remains plain PostgreSQL and skips this migration.

docs.title: Replication, failure and limits
docs.text:
What is it? Physical streaming replays WAL on a standby; promotion makes a standby writable. Failover is recovery after failure, not a backup.

Why Clichy uses it CNPG maintains two instances and redirects its read-write Service after promotion. Clients must reconnect; interrupted jobs may retry.

Two 2 GiB PVCs and the existing CPU/memory budgets are retained. Replication is asynchronous: recent commits may be lost if the primary fails before replay. All instances share valtask's disk/host; this is neither horizontal capacity scaling nor node-level availability. K3s 1.37 remains outside CNPG 1.30's officially supported matrix even though it is tested; the installer keeps its explicit gate.

Local disposable tests cover non-superuser SCRAM access, certificate-authenticated Citus COPY, logical restore, streaming and native PostgreSQL promotion with unchanged shard IDs and subsequent writes. CNPG-managed failover on Kubernetes is not yet verified. The healthcheck observes configuration, shards and active streaming; it deliberately skips failover testing. A logical dump restores rows/schema/history, not Citus distribution metadata: the target must be registered by the versioned migration after restore. Archives already recording that migration need the explicit reviewed recovery step in the runbook. Physical WAL replication preserves the target's catalog/shard IDs. Coordinated database/photo backups and a restore rehearsal are prerequisites to cutover. See ADR 0009 for the feasibility basis.

docs.title: Kubernetes and environments
docs.text:
What is it? Kubernetes schedules containers and manages Services, persistent volumes and workload controllers. K3s packages it for a small server with Traefik, local-path storage and Metrics Server.

Why Clichy uses it The same application manifests support namespace-specific configuration, rollouts and scaling on the intentionally single-node valtask.

docs.title: Environments and resources
docs.text:
Environment Namespace Application database Storage Dev clichy-dev CNPG Local-path; local cluster Test clichy-test CNPG + Citus target Local-path Production clichy-prod CNPG + Citus target Retained local PVs on valtask

infra/kubernetes/base defines Web/API/worker, Redis, photo storage and Ingress. overlays/{dev,test,prod} customize hosts, image names, configuration and replica counts. Their separate database subdirectories configure CNPG. Test/Production application overlays deliberately exclude databases so a routine release cannot change a database image. The old standalone Test manifests remain only for the pending migration/rollback checkpoint and are no longer applied by deployment. Separate namespaces and Secrets are logical isolation, not separate clusters or host-level availability.

docs.title: Prepare a server
docs.text:
These steps modify a host/cluster; review scripts before running them. No installation command is needed for normal local application development.

  1. Prepare Ubuntu Server 24.04 with hostname valtask, working SSH and a mounted /srv/clichy for Production. Install baseline tools using ordinary APT:
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install --no-install-recommends ca-certificates curl git gnupg jq openssl python3 tar ufw
  1. Configure Tailscale/MagicDNS and firewall policy. Verify tailscale ping valtask from an authorized client. Restrict ports 80, 3000 and 4466 to the intended private clients; existing UFW rules and SSH access require host-specific review.
  2. Run ./infra/kubernetes/scripts/install-k3s.sh as the non-root operator. It writes a mode-0600 kubeconfig, default ~/.kube/config-k3s; set KUBECONFIG to it explicitly and inspect kubectl get nodes. It does not alter firewall/SSH.
  3. Run ./infra/kubernetes/scripts/install-helm.sh if Helm is absent. Then run ./infra/kubernetes/cnpg/install-operator.sh before namespace preparation. The pinned K3s default is 1.37; the pinned CNPG installer treats that as tested but unsupported and requires the explicit CNPG_ALLOW_TESTED_UNSUPPORTED_K8S=1 acknowledgement. Do not silently bypass this check.
  4. Run ./infra/kubernetes/scripts/prepare-namespace.sh test (and prod when preparing Production). The script confirms the target, generates/reuses local mode-0600 secret files under ~/.config/clichy, normalizes the DB host/user, asks for GHCR read credentials, renders the database image for the checked-out published commit, creates isolated Secrets and waits for databases. For a fresh Test/Prod installation, apply Prisma migrations and acknowledge the validated architecture before the first application release. Existing environments must follow the cutover runbook instead of rerunning preparation to switch their Secrets early.
  5. Install monitoring and optionally Headlamp with their scripts. Use configure-lan-access.sh for the Traefik admin ports; it refuses to overwrite conflicting Traefik values. See scripts.
  6. Configure the self-hosted runner, then deploy through CI.

Namespace preparation can change Secrets; it is not a routine healthcheck. Test uses clichy-server-secrets, Production clichy-prod-secrets; each namespace also has clichy-postgres-app and ghcr-pull-secret. Never display their data in logs or copy credentials between environments.

docs.title: Persistent storage
docs.text:
API and worker share the 10 GiB clichy-server-photos claim at /data/photos; Redis has a 1 GiB claim. The old Test Citus claim remains retained for rollback. CNPG creates two separate 2 GiB claims per environment. Production pre-binds CNPG to local PVs under /srv/clichy/k3s-storage/prod/postgres-cnpg-{1,2}, with UID/GID 26, node affinity and Retain. Preparation refuses unsafe existing paths and requires the mount.

The old Production PostgreSQL PV/path remains reserved in the storage manifest; removing the unused old StatefulSet source does not delete that live volume. Do not delete/reuse it as part of normal deployment. ReadWriteOnce claims fit this one-node design; monitor actual disk use, not just declared PVC capacities. Retain, replicas and local-path storage are not backups.

The Dev overlay uses local :dev image tags; load locally built images into your chosen cluster yourself. The deploy.sh entry point is intentionally restricted to Test/Production on valtask.

docs.title: Portability
docs.text: A cloud move would retain application images and namespace isolation, but replace valtask-bound local PVs with provider storage and supply a shared photo volume accessible to API/worker. Review ingress/DNS/tunnel endpoints, Secrets, runner kubeconfig, node assumptions in deploy/migrate and CNPG storage classes together. Restore a coordinated backup into an isolated environment and validate before cutover. No cloud overlay or tested migration automation is provided.

docs.title: Redis and BullMQ
docs.text:
What is it? Redis stores in-memory data with optional persistence; BullMQ uses Redis to coordinate queued jobs, retries and worker delivery.

Why Clichy uses it Image processing runs outside the API request lifecycle. The PostgreSQL outbox keeps unpublished work durable when Redis is unavailable.

Each namespace has one Redis Deployment, AOF and a 1 GiB PVC, with noeviction and a 256 MiB memory budget. It is internal, not a replicated cache. Queue names/credentials must agree between API and worker. See the photo lifecycle for recovery and retry semantics.

docs.title: Prometheus and Grafana
docs.text:
What is it? Prometheus scrapes time-series metrics and evaluates rules; Grafana displays them. Exporters expose measurements; ServiceMonitor/PodMonitor resources tell Prometheus where to scrape.

Why Clichy uses it Operators need HTTP latency/error rate, queue backlog, worker failures, disk capacity and PostgreSQL replication visibility.

install-monitoring.sh installs the pinned kube-prometheus-stack chart into monitoring. Versioned Helm values, monitors, rules and the Clichy Photo Service dashboard live under infra/kubernetes/monitoring. The ordinary Test workflow applies monitoring manifests without upgrading Helm. Re-running the installer for an existing release requires a reviewed explicit upgrade.

Source Discovery and useful signals API /metrics ServiceMonitor; HTTP rate/status/duration and unpublished outbox Worker /metrics PodMonitor; BullMQ state, attempts, duration and query health CNPG metrics PodMonitor; PostgreSQL WAL/replication Node and Kubernetes exporters CPU/memory, PVC usage, Pod restarts and availability

Open private Grafana at http://valtask:3000, select the environment and inspect the dashboard. Verify Prometheus → Status → Targets before interpreting an empty panel as idle. Rules cover backlog, missing scrapes, unavailable workloads, restarts, resource pressure, storage and HPA limits. Retention is seven days. Headlamp at http://valtask:4466 is optional private cluster administration.

docs.title: HPA and Metrics Server
docs.text:
What is it? HPA adjusts Deployment replica counts from observed metrics. Metrics Server supplies the Kubernetes resource metrics API used for CPU scaling; Prometheus is a separate monitoring system.

Why Clichy uses it Test Web/API can scale from one to four replicas at 70% of requested CPU. Worker, Redis and databases do not have HPAs.

Verify kubectl top pods -n clichy-test and kubectl get hpa -n clichy-test before load testing. An <unknown> metric needs investigation, not more load. For a bounded, confirmed Test-only load demonstration:

./infra/kubernetes/scripts/load-test-test.sh server 300 32
# Or use web instead of server.
kubectl get hpa -n clichy-test -w

The generator uses unauthenticated reads (API 401 is expected), creates local load and a temporary port-forward, and never uploads data. Observe sampling delays and wait for scale-down afterwards. Do not manually scale HPA-controlled Deployments. For a manual worker demonstration use kubectl scale deployment/clichy-worker -n clichy-test --replicas=2, then restore --replicas=1; this changes cluster resource usage. Extra replicas on one node do not add physical capacity or node-level availability.

docs.title: Deployment and migrations
docs.text:
What is it? Deployment rolls out application images; migration evolves schema. Database image preparation is a separate, deliberately approved operation.

Why Clichy uses it Matching commit/image SHAs, namespace Secrets and migration-before-application ordering protect releases and existing data.

docs.title: Normal operation after cutover
docs.text:
Pushes to master deploy Test after CI. Production requires manual dispatch with deploy_prod=true and its GitHub environment protections. From a clean checkout matching published images, deploy.sh test|prod sha-<40-hex> verifies valtask/SHA, confirms, checks CNPG, migrates, renders exact-SHA application manifests and waits for Web/API/worker rollouts. It does not update the database image or apply the old standalone Citus resources. CI explicitly sets CLICHY_DEPLOY_CONFIRM=yes.

Both application/migration connections use clichy-postgres-rw. migrate.sh <env> status is a Prisma diagnostic; migrate.sh <env> deploy applies pending SQL via an ephemeral loopback port-forward. The script validates the Secret's host/base without printing its URL and cleans processes/credentials. Loopback forwarding uses sslmode=disable for SCRAM; Citus's internal connections use certificates. A migration failure prevents application rollout. Applied SQL remains immutable.

The one-time clichy.io/database-architecture=cnpg-citus-v1 Cluster acknowledgement is required before a release may proceed. It prevents an ordinary push from silently choosing the old, unrelated Test CNPG database. Until the controlled cutover below is complete, this explicit refusal is expected.

docs.title: Controlled cutover
docs.text: Operator procedure, not commands already executed. Test first, Production only after Test restoration, application processing and CNPG switchover are verified. The operations below pause service, modify databases/Secrets and may change the primary. They require explicit approval, a maintenance window, verified database and photos backups, enough disk space, and a clean published checkout. No backup has yet been confirmed from valtask. Do not run the whole page unattended.

docs.title: 1. Publish and prepare backups
docs.text:
Let CI build/test/package the reviewed commit. Its database image is ghcr.io/valatras/clichy-postgres:18.6-citus14.2.0-sha-<commit>. The Test deployment is intentionally blocked by the acknowledgement until cutover. Do not manually dispatch Production as a shortcut.

For one environment at a time, start with NS=clichy-test (later clichy-prod). Save original replica counts and stop writers; this causes application downtime. The zero replica setting suspends HPA activity until explicitly scaled back up.

set -euo pipefail
NS=clichy-test
test "$(kubectl get nodes -o 'jsonpath={range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}{end}')" = valtask || { echo 'Expected only valtask'; exit 1; }
umask 077
BACKUP_DIR="$HOME/clichy-backups/$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)-$NS"
mkdir -p "$BACKUP_DIR"
printf '%s\n' "$NS" > "$BACKUP_DIR/namespace"
kubectl get deployment clichy-server clichy-worker -n "$NS" -o yaml > "$BACKUP_DIR/writers.yaml"
kubectl get cluster.postgresql.cnpg.io clichy-postgres -n "$NS" -o yaml > "$BACKUP_DIR/cluster.yaml"
# Credential backup: protected file only; do not display or share it.
secret=clichy-server-secrets
[ "$NS" != clichy-prod ] || secret=clichy-prod-secrets
kubectl get secret "$secret" -n "$NS" -o json > "$BACKUP_DIR/app-secret.json"
kubectl scale deployment/clichy-server deployment/clichy-worker -n "$NS" --replicas=0
kubectl wait --for=delete pod -n "$NS" -l app=clichy-server --timeout=180s
kubectl wait --for=delete pod -n "$NS" -l app=clichy-worker --timeout=180s
primary="$(kubectl get cluster.postgresql.cnpg.io clichy-postgres -n "$NS" -o 'jsonpath={.status.currentPrimary}')"
db=clichy_test
[ "$NS" != clichy-prod ] || db=clichy_prod
kubectl exec -n "$NS" "$primary" -c postgres -- pg_dump -U postgres -Fc -d "$db" > "$BACKUP_DIR/cnpg.dump"
if [ "$NS" = clichy-test ]; then
  kubectl exec -n "$NS" deployment/clichy-citus -c postgres -- pg_dump -U clichy -Fc -d clichy_test > "$BACKUP_DIR/active-citus.dump"
fi

Stop on any failed command; never treat a partial dump as a backup. Both Test sources must be backed up: the inactive CNPG database has a distinct row/history. The active Citus dump is the source for the new application database.

Back up the quiesced photos volume through a temporary read-only Pod. This Pod uses the already-deployed application image, contains no application Secret env, and is deleted afterwards; the PVC is never deleted.

image="$(kubectl get deployment clichy-server -n "$NS" -o 'jsonpath={.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image}')"
kubectl run photo-backup -n "$NS" --image="$image" --restart=Never --override-type=strategic \
  --overrides='{"spec":{"imagePullSecrets":[{"name":"ghcr-pull-secret"}],"securityContext":{"runAsNonRoot":true,"runAsUser":10001,"runAsGroup":2000,"supplementalGroups":[1000]},"containers":[{"name":"photo-backup","volumeMounts":[{"name":"photos","mountPath":"/data/photos","readOnly":true}]}],"volumes":[{"name":"photos","persistentVolumeClaim":{"claimName":"clichy-server-photos","readOnly":true}}]}}' \
  --command -- sleep 3600
kubectl wait pod/photo-backup -n "$NS" --for=condition=Ready --timeout=120s
kubectl exec -n "$NS" photo-backup -- tar -C /data/photos -cf - . > "$BACKUP_DIR/photos.tar"
kubectl delete pod photo-backup -n "$NS" --wait=true
tar -tf "$BACKUP_DIR/photos.tar" >/dev/null
kubectl exec -i -n "$NS" "$primary" -c postgres -- pg_restore --list < "$BACKUP_DIR/cnpg.dump" >/dev/null
(cd "$BACKUP_DIR" && sha256sum *.dump photos.tar > SHA256SUMS && sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS)

Archive listing/checksums do not replace a restore rehearsal. Copy/encrypt the backups off valtask and verify restoration before proceeding. If the window is aborted, restore the original writer replica counts; no database cutover has occurred. Do not restore Secrets or whole workload YAML blindly onto newer state.

docs.title: 2. Prepare the Citus-capable CNPG image
docs.text:
Keep writers stopped. From the clean checkout that CI packaged, render and server-dry-run only the database overlay, then inspect the result. Applying it is a separate approved operation: it updates images/configuration and restarts instances, preserving their existing PVCs. Acknowledge the existing Kubernetes 1.37/CNPG support limitation separately; do not weaken the installer gate.

test "$(cat "$BACKUP_DIR/namespace")" = "$NS"
env_name="${NS#clichy-}"
release_sha="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
test -z "$(git status --porcelain)" || { echo 'Use a clean reviewed checkout'; exit 1; }
kubectl kustomize "infra/kubernetes/overlays/$env_name/database" |
  sed "s/REPLACE_WITH_TESTED_GIT_SHA/$release_sha/g" > "$BACKUP_DIR/database-target.yaml"
kubectl apply --dry-run=server -f "$BACKUP_DIR/database-target.yaml"
# Only after reviewing the dry-run and approving the rolling database update:
kubectl apply -f "$BACKUP_DIR/database-target.yaml"
kubectl wait -n "$NS" --for=condition=Ready cluster.postgresql.cnpg.io/clichy-postgres --timeout=900s
primary="$(kubectl get cluster.postgresql.cnpg.io clichy-postgres -n "$NS" -o 'jsonpath={.status.currentPrimary}')"
kubectl exec -n "$NS" "$primary" -c postgres -- psql -X -U postgres -d postgres -c "SHOW shared_preload_libraries; SELECT application_name,state FROM pg_stat_replication; SELECT rolname,rolsuper,rolreplication FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname='clichy';"

The last output must show Citus first, a streaming standby and a non-superuser/non-replication clichy role. Stop if those conditions differ; role changes are not automatic. Verify actual operator-generated certificates and loopback authentication during restoration. Do not proceed on an admission, image, preload or replication error.

docs.title: 3. Test: import without overwriting the old CNPG database
docs.text:
Create a new staging database; an existing name causes a safe stop. Restore the active Citus archive as postgres, preserving object ownership and every Prisma history row. The existing clichy role stays non-superuser; pg_dump does not restore role attributes. Do not run Prisma migrations while the staging name is in use: environment-guarded SQL must run only after the canonical name is restored.

First verify that the two existing namespace credentials agree, without displaying them. A mismatch requires diagnosis before renaming databases or changing Secrets:

kubectl get secret clichy-server-secrets clichy-postgres-app -n clichy-test -o json |
python3 -c '
import base64,json,sys
from urllib.parse import urlsplit,unquote
items={x["metadata"]["name"]:x["data"] for x in json.load(sys.stdin)["items"]}
u=urlsplit(base64.b64decode(items["clichy-server-secrets"]["DATABASE_URL"]).decode())
p=base64.b64decode(items["clichy-postgres-app"]["password"]).decode()
assert u.username=="clichy" and unquote(u.password or "")==p, "Credential mismatch: stop; no values displayed"
print("PASS namespace credential consistency")'

test "$NS" = clichy-test
test "$(cat "$BACKUP_DIR/namespace")" = "$NS"
kubectl exec -n clichy-test "$primary" -c postgres -- createdb -U postgres -O clichy clichy_test_import
kubectl exec -n clichy-test "$primary" -c postgres -- psql -X -U postgres -d clichy_test_import -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -c 'CREATE EXTENSION citus;'
kubectl exec -i -n clichy-test "$primary" -c postgres -- pg_restore -U postgres --exit-on-error -d clichy_test_import < "$BACKUP_DIR/active-citus.dump"
kubectl exec -n clichy-test "$primary" -c postgres -- psql -X -U postgres -d clichy_test_import -c 'SELECT count(*) FROM "Photo"; SELECT migration_name,finished_at,rolled_back_at FROM "_prisma_migrations" ORDER BY migration_name;'

Compare counts, all migration rows (including the rolled-back attempt) and keys/FKs with the source. A logical pg_dump restores ordinary tables and their rows, not Citus distribution catalogs. Do not claim sharding is restored at this point: the still-pending new migration will register the restored tables after the canonical name switch. Original source tables/shards remain untouched. Retain the old Test CNPG database and its one-row dataset under a different name. The following switch terminates connections to both Test databases; no rows, tables or PVCs are dropped.

kubectl exec -i -n clichy-test "$primary" -c postgres -- psql -X -U postgres -d postgres -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 <<'SQL'
DO $$ BEGIN IF EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM pg_database WHERE datname='clichy_test_before_unify') THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'Retained database name already exists; inspect first'; END IF; END $$;
ALTER DATABASE clichy_test ALLOW_CONNECTIONS false;
ALTER DATABASE clichy_test_import ALLOW_CONNECTIONS false;
SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid,10000) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE datname IN ('clichy_test','clichy_test_import');
ALTER DATABASE clichy_test RENAME TO clichy_test_before_unify;
ALTER DATABASE clichy_test_import RENAME TO clichy_test;
ALTER DATABASE clichy_test ALLOW_CONNECTIONS true;
SQL

Update only Test's Secret database hostname, preserving credentials and database name. The JSON patch flows directly into kubectl; do not add shell tracing or print intermediate values. Keep the protected Secret backup for rollback.

kubectl get secret clichy-server-secrets -n clichy-test -o json |
python3 -c '
import base64,json,sys
from urllib.parse import urlsplit,urlunsplit
s=json.load(sys.stdin); u=urlsplit(base64.b64decode(s["data"]["DATABASE_URL"]).decode())
assert u.scheme in ("postgres","postgresql") and u.hostname == "clichy-citus-rw" and u.path == "/clichy_test" and u.username == "clichy" and u.password is not None, "Unexpected source endpoint; stop"
credentials=u.netloc.rsplit("@",1)[0]
value=urlunsplit((u.scheme,credentials+"@clichy-postgres-rw:5432",u.path,u.query,u.fragment))
json.dump([{"op":"replace","path":"/data/DATABASE_URL","value":base64.b64encode(value.encode()).decode()}],sys.stdout)
' | kubectl patch secret clichy-server-secrets -n clichy-test --type=json --patch-file=/dev/stdin
./infra/kubernetes/scripts/migrate.sh test deploy

The new migration must now establish the 32 colocated shards without changing row counts or prior history. The original Citus shard IDs need not be the IDs allocated in this new logical copy. Once established, WAL promotion must preserve the target's shard IDs; do not confuse these two kinds of transition.

docs.title: 4. Production: preserve the database and align its schema
docs.text:
Only after Test's checkpoints succeed, repeat backup/write-pause/image preparation for NS=clichy-prod. Its endpoint already uses CNPG; no import or Secret host change is needed. Existing-cluster bootstrap SQL is not rerun, so create the extension explicitly, then apply the new additive migration as the non-superuser application role through the existing helper:

test "$NS" = clichy-prod
test "$(cat "$BACKUP_DIR/namespace")" = "$NS"
kubectl exec -n clichy-prod "$primary" -c postgres -- psql -X -U postgres -d clichy_prod -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -c 'CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS citus;'
./infra/kubernetes/scripts/migrate.sh prod deploy

Production conversion takes table locks and redistributes rows into new logical shards within its transaction. Downtime is intentional; no zero-downtime promise is made. Null owners are backfilled; irreconcilable rows or unexpected node metadata stop the migration. Do not mark it applied blindly or modify historical SQL.

docs.title: 5. Verify, resume and acknowledge
docs.text:
Restore the original writer replica counts (normally one each), then run the healthcheck from this checkout. Test also needs an authenticated photo upload, processing/thumbnail check, and a controlled CNPG switchover before Production. The switchover command requires the official kubectl CNPG plugin and explicit approval: it changes leadership, drops existing connections and may lose unreceived async commits if treated as forced failover. Pause writes and verify catch-up first.

kubectl scale deployment/clichy-server deployment/clichy-worker -n "$NS" --replicas=1
./infra/kubernetes/scripts/healthcheck.sh "${NS#clichy-}"
# Approved Test-only controlled switchover, after replica catch-up:
kubectl get pods -n clichy-test -l cnpg.io/cluster=clichy-postgres -L cnpg.io/instanceRole
standby="$(kubectl get pods -n clichy-test -l cnpg.io/cluster=clichy-postgres,cnpg.io/instanceRole=replica -o 'jsonpath={.items[0].metadata.name}')"
test -n "$standby"
kubectl cnpg promote clichy-postgres "$standby" -n clichy-test
kubectl wait -n clichy-test --for="jsonpath={.status.currentPrimary}=$standby" cluster.postgresql.cnpg.io/clichy-postgres --timeout=900s
kubectl wait -n clichy-test --for=condition=Ready cluster.postgresql.cnpg.io/clichy-postgres --timeout=900s
./infra/kubernetes/scripts/healthcheck.sh test
# Only after data/history, application and certificate checks pass:
kubectl annotate cluster.postgresql.cnpg.io clichy-postgres -n "$NS" \
  clichy.io/database-architecture=cnpg-citus-v1 --overwrite

Confirm primary name changed, the -rw Service follows it, shard IDs/row counts/FKs are unchanged, streaming resumes, and reads/writes/processing work. Record the actual evidence: the healthcheck does not perform this test. A controlled switchover is not an automatic failure-recovery demonstration. Once acknowledged, rerun the failed Test deployment job. Production remains a separate manual action.

After successful, operator-confirmed Test cutover, retire the old standalone Deployment/Service and remove infra/kubernetes/citus from the active repository. Those four files are currently retained for rollback and are no longer referenced by normal deployment. Do not remove its PVC, the retained Test database or backups. No automatic pruning is enabled. After that explicit checkpoint, cluster cleanup can remove only the two obsolete resources (never kubectl delete -k, which would also delete the PVC):

kubectl delete deployment/clichy-citus service/clichy-citus-rw -n clichy-test

Repository cleanup is a subsequent reviewed source change, after the operator confirms migration/rollback validation; do not edit the clean server checkout in place or delete the retained claim.

docs.title: Rollback
docs.text:
Before schema conversion, an error means stop and inspect; preserve all backups and original connection details. If a rename step is interrupted, inspect the existing names and ALLOW_CONNECTIONS flags before enabling the intended database.

A failed transactional migration rolls back its DDL/data changes, but Prisma may record a failed attempt. Diagnose first; use Prisma resolve only for the specific inspected failure, not an old hard-coded repair.

Before new writes resume, Test can restore its original endpoint without touching CNPG data: kubectl apply -f "$BACKUP_DIR/app-secret.json", keep/restart the old Citus Deployment, restore writer counts and remove the acknowledgement with kubectl annotate cluster.postgresql.cnpg.io clichy-postgres -n clichy-test clichy.io/database-architecture-.

After committed Production DDL, retain the Citus-capable image. Restore cnpg.dump into a new database (created with owner clichy) using the same createdb/pg_restore steps above, verify it, pause writers, and perform the same two-database name switch from postgres, retaining the failed target under a different unused name. Do not use --clean, delete PVCs or downgrade to an image missing Citus while Citus databases remain. After any post-cutover writes, restoring an older snapshot would lose those writes: reconcile them before choosing rollback. The photos archive belongs to the same backup point; never overwrite live photo storage blindly.

For a Production restore rollback, keep writers at zero and choose unused names:

NS=clichy-prod
primary="$(kubectl get cluster.postgresql.cnpg.io clichy-postgres -n "$NS" -o 'jsonpath={.status.currentPrimary}')"
kubectl exec -n "$NS" "$primary" -c postgres -- createdb -U postgres -O clichy clichy_prod_restore
kubectl exec -i -n "$NS" "$primary" -c postgres -- pg_restore -U postgres --exit-on-error -d clichy_prod_restore < "$BACKUP_DIR/cnpg.dump"
# Verify restored counts, keys and migration history BEFORE the name switch.
kubectl exec -i -n "$NS" "$primary" -c postgres -- psql -X -U postgres -d postgres -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 <<'SQL'
DO $$ BEGIN IF EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM pg_database WHERE datname='clichy_prod_after_failed_unify') THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'Retained name exists; inspect first'; END IF; END $$;
ALTER DATABASE clichy_prod ALLOW_CONNECTIONS false;
ALTER DATABASE clichy_prod_restore ALLOW_CONNECTIONS false;
SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid,10000) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE datname IN ('clichy_prod','clichy_prod_restore');
ALTER DATABASE clichy_prod RENAME TO clichy_prod_after_failed_unify;
ALTER DATABASE clichy_prod_restore RENAME TO clichy_prod;
ALTER DATABASE clichy_prod ALLOW_CONNECTIONS true;
SQL
kubectl annotate cluster.postgresql.cnpg.io clichy-postgres -n "$NS" clichy.io/database-architecture-
# Restore the original writer counts only after validating the restored database.

docs.title: Logical backups taken after unification
docs.text:
A post-cutover archive already records migration 20261117140000 as applied, yet still does not contain Citus distribution catalogs. A plain restore followed by migrate deploy alone is therefore insufficient. On a restored, isolated copy with its canonical database name, after reviewing the archived schema/version, replay the same immutable migration SQL explicitly to reconstruct/validate layout without rewriting Prisma history:

# State-changing restore recovery, not routine deployment or healthchecking.
# NS, primary and db must identify the reviewed restored copy, with writers paused.
kubectl exec -i -n "$NS" "$primary" -c postgres -- psql -X -U postgres -d "$db" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1   < packages/db/prisma/migrations/20261117140000_unified_cnpg_citus/migration.sql

Verify counts, FKs, ownership, migration history and sharding before resuming. This uses the existing versioned SQL, not a second registration script. Never replay an old layout against a newer schema without review. Physical backups preserve catalogs and shard IDs; a production CNPG backup/recovery provider and its restore rehearsal remain operational work, not an automation delivered here.

docs.title: Scripts & Commands
docs.text:
What is it? These are the supported operational entry points and their side effects. Commands assume the repository root and an explicitly selected kubeconfig; scripts never make choosing the correct environment unnecessary.

Why Clichy uses it Routine observations, installation, deployment and load testing should have clear responsibilities and predictable impact.

docs.title: Public scripts
docs.text:
Paths below scripts/ are relative to infra/kubernetes/.

Script / command Purpose Environment Impact scripts/install-k3s.sh Install K3s; prepare operator kubeconfig New Ubuntu 24.04 host Changes host/services; confirms install scripts/install-helm.sh Install Helm with checked APT configuration Ubuntu/Debian Changes host packages; confirms cnpg/install-operator.sh Install pinned CNPG operator Cluster Applies CRDs/operator after compatibility checks scripts/prepare-namespace.sh dev\|test\|prod Prepare Secrets, storage paths and databases Local Dev / valtask Test/Prod Changes namespace and local secret files; confirms scripts/configure-lan-access.sh Set Traefik private admin entrypoints valtask Changes cluster networking; confirms, rejects conflicts scripts/install-monitoring.sh Install Prometheus/Grafana Cluster Helm/Secrets/manifests; confirms; existing release needs explicit upgrade flag scripts/install-headlamp.sh Install private Headlamp Cluster Helm/manifests/RBAC; confirms scripts/deploy.sh test\|prod sha-<40-hex> Migrate then roll out matching images Test/Prod Changes database/workloads; confirms scripts/migrate.sh test\|prod deploy Apply pending Prisma migrations Test/Prod Changes database scripts/migrate.sh test\|prod status Full Prisma history diagnostic Test/Prod Database reads; Secret access and temporary loopback port-forward scripts/healthcheck.sh test\|prod [--verbose] Observe environment invariants Test/Prod Read-only Kubernetes/SQL/HTTP/Redis observations scripts/load-test-test.sh server\|web 300 32 Bounded scaling demonstration Test only HTTP load and temporary port-forward; confirms pnpm --filter server backfill:photos Reschedule incomplete library processing Configured API environment Changes database/queue; build first; review target

Bash/Node test files are internal checks, not admin commands. Baseline host APT setup is documented directly in Kubernetes setup, without a separate wrapper. No active script performs the old empty-table repair.

Database image preparation is explicit; application deployment is blocked until the cutover acknowledgement exists.

docs.title: Healthchecks
docs.text:
./infra/kubernetes/scripts/healthcheck.sh test
./infra/kubernetes/scripts/healthcheck.sh prod
./infra/kubernetes/scripts/healthcheck.sh test --verbose

Requires Bash, kubectl and GNU timeout (Ubuntu coreutils). No local database client or pnpm is needed. Kubernetes read/exec permissions are required; Secrets and connection strings are not fetched. Use the checkout whose migration names you expect in the environment. The script keeps the current context unchanged.

Scope Checks Both Namespace, available Web/API/worker/Redis, PVCs, Redis PING, internal API HTTP, expected CNPG endpoint and a read-only SQL probe from the API Pod using its own credentials Both databases Two ready CNPG instances, primary/replica, connectivity, non-privileged app role, Citus extension/preload, local coordinator, hash(userId), 32 colocated shards per table, compound primary keys, validated FKs, migration history and active streaming Failover Explicit SKIP: requires an approved state-changing exercise

Each kubectl operation is bounded by a 10-second request and 25-second outer limit; rollout/wait is 15 seconds. SQL forces read-only mode and a 10-second statement timeout. Total runtime is the sum of checks. Raw command errors are suppressed even in verbose mode to avoid disclosure; verbose prints target scope. For detailed investigation use troubleshooting.

Example (abbreviated, not a live observation):

PASS Kubernetes namespace access
PASS Citus reference table, hash(userId), 32 shards and colocation
WARN Migration checks compare names only; checksum drift requires Prisma migrate status
Summary: PASS=31 WARN=1 FAIL=0 SKIP=1

Exit 0: no failed checks (warnings/skips allowed). Exit 1: failed check or missing dependency. Exit 2: invalid arguments. Missing required components fail. Migration-name comparison does not prove checksum equality or detect all extra history; use migrate.sh <env> status for Prisma's full comparison.

Internal HTTP is called from an API Pod; deployment probes cover Web/worker. This does not test public ingress, authentication, uploads, storage writes or job completion. Before the controlled cutover, the new target checks correctly fail on the old split topology rather than pretending it is unified. Healthchecks never apply resources, run migrations, delete data or repair state.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
What is it? Diagnostics collect evidence about an unhealthy component. Recovery changes state and must be planned from that evidence.

Why Clichy uses it A failed Pod, migration or queue should not lead to unrelated changes, discarded data or a retry of an obsolete incident repair.

Start with healthcheck.sh test|prod, then inspect only the affected namespace:

kubectl config current-context
kubectl get deployments,pods,services,pvc,ingress -n clichy-test -o wide
kubectl get events -n clichy-test --sort-by=.lastTimestamp
kubectl logs deployment/clichy-server -n clichy-test --tail=100
kubectl logs deployment/clichy-worker -n clichy-test --tail=100

These reads may contain user data in logs; redact before sharing. Replace the namespace deliberately for Production.

Symptom Investigate Local client/types missing pnpm install, pnpm db:generate, pnpm env:generate; verify Node/pnpm versions and environment schemas Local DB/Redis refused docker compose ps from packages/db; check 5432/6379 and the selected .env Login fails Auth URL, browser origin, secret length and cookies; API/Web host assumptions Pod/PVC Pending kubectl describe pod / pvc; StorageClass, free space, PV affinity, mounted paths and Production UID 26 ImagePullBackOff Exact SHA tag, image publication and namespace pull-secret presence/type; never print Secret values API database failure Both: CNPG+Citus, primary and clichy-postgres-rw; inspect endpoints and run migration status Migration/layout failure Read migration error and current catalogs; no reset, drop, automatic redistribution or blind resolve Upload 400/413 Supported format, 20 MiB upload cap and 40-million-pixel decoder limit Photo remains PENDING/PROCESSING Worker /ready probe/logs, Redis, queue name, outbox rows, common storage; allow documented stale-recovery intervals Missing thumbnail Owner, completed state and same original/derivative filesystem for API/worker Empty Grafana panel Prometheus targets and ServiceMonitor/PodMonitor discovery before assuming no traffic HPA <unknown> kubectl top pods -n clichy-test, Metrics APIService, HPA events and CPU requests; Prometheus is separate Public/private URL unavailable DNS/Host header, tunnel for Prod, Traefik entrypoint/class, Service endpoints and firewall

For CNPG inspect kubectl describe cluster clichy-postgres -n clichy-prod and operator logs in cnpg-system. For Citus inspect the primary's logs, extension/preload and pg_dist_partition / pg_dist_shard metadata. Loopback authentication failures during COPY need the CNPG certificate mapping, not a trust rule. Before cutover the legacy Test sources are distinct; follow the runbook.

A missing streaming standby does not by itself justify deleting a Pod or PVC. An incorrect historical Citus registration needs an inspected data-preserving migration plan. The old empty-table repair and hard-coded Prisma resolve mode are removed; Git history retains their context. Do not revive them as a generic repair. Verify coordinated database/photo backups before any state-changing recovery. No tested turnkey restore or automatic rollback exists.

For runner failures, inspect its GitHub Online/Idle state and service logs (sudo journalctl -u 'actions.runner*' --since '30 minutes ago'), then verify its actual account can access the configured kubeconfig and tools.
